The program SIR allows the definition of three-dimensional sections through an arbitrary struc- ture. Then the following tasks are performed in this section:
• Representation of the intersected elements (TRUS, BEAM, CABL, QUAD, BRIC, SPRI) and the graphical representation of their results
• Calculation of the resultant forces and moments including the support reactions
• Output of a data record for the dimensioning of the section with the program AQB consisting of:
– thin-walled cross section parts (from QUAD elements)
– thick-walled cross section parts (fom QUAD and BRIC elements)
Thus SIR may be used for the check of FE calculations concerning the global equilibrium and for the visualisation of the results.

On the other side SIR is an important link for the design of FE structures in the ultimate limit state. The standard FE design codes treat every element individually and do not fulfill the global compatibility of those strain states. This may lead to uneconomical or unsure results dependently on the problem.

A consistent analysis with the limit load theory requests a considerable CPU time. If the user does not want to consider this, SIR allows to apply a classic beam design also for plane struc- tures by excising of reasonable subsystems. In this case a global ultimate limit state can be verified.
SIR generates cross sections and internal forces and moments which can be used directly by the programs AQUA and AQB or AQBS.

First the section plane is defined. This contains a local coordinate system which corresponds to a beam coordiante system. A "‘beam"’ number and an abscissa X are used for the designation of the plane.

First SIR determines the elements which are intersected by the defined section plane. In this case the limits at which it is possible to intersect are considered in the local coordinate system of the section.

Then the stress state at the intersection area element - section plane is determined for the intersected elements. In this case a linear stress distribution in the element based at the results in the Gauss points is placed as a basis. The internal forces and moments of the element at the intersection area are calculated from the stress state via an integration.

Forces of axial symmetric systems are calculated per m circumference (=QUAD thickness). SIR integrates at a circle sector. The QUAD thickness increases in radial direction. The thick- ness at cuts reference point is 1 m.
The internal forces and moments at the intersection point beam - plane are determined with a cubic interpolation for the intersected beam and truss elements.
SIR calculates the resultant forces and moments around the reference point after the transfor- mation of the internal forces into the local coordinate system.

SIR is saving all forces in the database directly. Maybe the reference point is not equal to the centre of gravity of the new generated cross section. In this case additional moments are calculated due to normal force * lever arm (= distance between reference point and centre of gravity of the cross section). The reference point position should be checked therefore before further processing, e.g. a design calculation with program AQB. Perhaps the calculation has to be repeated with an adapted reference point. With the program WinGRAF it is possible to perform this iterative step interactively. Otherwise the generated input file (.SR) should be running, so that AQB may transforme all forces into the centre of gravity of cross section.

Tendon forces lead to a stress level in the whole area element. But the tendon forces are missed during the integration of forces and moments if the cut do not hit the tendon. This could lead to unexpected results (jumps). SIR displays a warning in this case.

As an further option SIR adds all support reactions in a box which is defined via a section plane and an area in front of that and behind that. All nodes and elastic bedded elements within this area, depending on the control with ECHO REAC, are used for this purpose.
The input occurs in a free format with the CADINP input language (see the general manual SOFiSTiK: ’Basics’).
Three categories of units are distinguished:
mm Fixed unit. Input is always required in the specified unit.
[mm] Explicit unit. Input defaults to the specified unit. Alternatively, an explicit as- signment of a related unit is possible (eg. 2.5[m] ).

[mm]1011 Implicit unit. Implicit units are categorised semantically and denoted by a cor- responding identity number (shown in green). Valid categories referring to the unit ”length” are, for example, geodetic elevation, section length and thickness. The default unit for each category is defined by the currently active (design code specific) unit set. This input default can be overridden as described above. The specified unit in square brackets corresponds to the default for unit set 5 (Eu- rocodes, NORM UNIT 5).

Input to CTRL AQUA and CTRL AQB
The results of SIR can be stored in an input file for the programs AQUA and AQB for the use
of a classical beam design. The kind and the extent of these dates are described with the corresponding CTRL options.

If nothing is input for CTRL AQUA, CTRL AQUA 2 is used as default if BRIC elements were found in database. The same default is set if the first cut beam cross section is thick-walled. Otherwise CTRL AQUA 1 is used as default for sections with beams, trusses or cables. The default of sections which intersect only QUAD elements is CTRL AQUA 2. In the case of curved structures the QUAD elements can be intersected each other. Because such intersection is unrepresentable for solid elements in AQUA, it is recommended to use CTRL AQUA 1.
The stress points ’Z-’ and ’Z+’ are generated as default of CTRL SPT for thickwalled cross sections.

For SIR, it is relatively difficult to find a suitable default of CTRL TOLG / TOLP for any system. Unfortunately, the oriention to the system dimensions is not possible, because even in a large system there can be areas with very small elements that are to be cut. This leads to very short polygonal edges. A too large CTRL TOLP (= maximum length of polygon edges in the gener- ated cross-section) causes these edges to disappear completely, which can lead to unusable cross-sections. Therefore it is sometimes more useful to set the geometrical tolerance of the cuts with CTRL TOLG more wide / finer. Then the decision for one of the two found QUAD elements is more clearly when cutting nearby QUAD edges.
Instead of an input with SECT in the program AQUA for every section the cross section num- bers can be defined also in a pure monotonic way with respect to this number via CTRL SMIN.
SIR calculates the sum of a QUAD reinforcement determined by BEMESS with CTRL LCR > 0 and ECHO REIN YES/FULL.

A four-digit number nnnn can be defined for the line type. The meaning is described in detail in the general manual SOFiSTiK: ’FEA / STRUCTURAL Installation and Basics’. The last digit means e.g.:
1 = solid 6 = tight dots 2 = dashed 7 = tight dots and dashes 3 = dotted 8 = spaced dashes 4 = dots and dashes 9 = spaced dots 5 = tight dashes
The first digit describes the pen number. For example the line type 3003 draws a dotted line with the third pen (green). Default of the colours:
1 = black or white 5 = yellow 2 = red 3 = green 7 = cyan 4 = blue 8 = brown

Only the elements with the selected group numbers are considered for the integration of the internal stresses and moments. The default is the use of all group numbers. The default NO is set for all groups with the input of the first record GRP.
If LAY is defined, the TRUSS and QUAD reinforcements are used as reinforcement with this layer for the cross section descriptions.
The group number of an element is equal to the element number divided by the group divisor (see program SOFiMSHA).
Item Description Unit Default NO Load case number − ! CSMI Addition of the statically determinate parts of the pre- − - stress for the tendons with the construction stages CSMI and CSMA CSMA − CSMI
The integration of the stresses and moments is performed in every following defined section for every selected load case.

The statically determinate parts of the prestress are determined from the selected tendons with CSMI and CSMA. These parts are added to the resultant internal forces and moments. Without this option the prestress is the inherent stress state. It means that only the statically indeterminate parts of the prestress remain in the resultant internal forces and moments.
In program ASE it is possible to calculate difference load cases from the sum load cases (CTRL DIFF ...).

The losts due to creep and shrinkage (without prestressing steel) of these difference load cases are necessary for the design with program AQB. They should be calculated therefore with the program SIR in order to prevent a new creep calculation in AQB.
In the program ASE the results of these difference load cases are saved in a special way in order to consider only the concrete part. Thus SIR ignores the part of the prestressing steel.
The SIR results of the difference load cases are therefore not equal to the simple difference of the initial (sum) load cases (because the part of the prestressing steel is not available).
You can find an example for that with more hints in program TEDDY at csm4_quad_singlespan.dat
In program ASE the construction stage creep and shrinkage 15 (CS 15) is stored in load case 4015 (LC 4015) (=sum load case for creep and shrinkage).
Then in ASE the difference load case 5015 (=difference load case creep and shrinkage) is created by using the control LC DIFF 1000 (an automatic procedure in program CSM).
Now in SIR only the difference load cases (LC 5015) should be used for calculation. Note that the construction stages input (LC CSMI) has to be used for load cases with prestress.

In each case a section is defined with SECT. An evaluation of the geometry and the internal forces occurs for all sections within an input block for all the defined load cases and groups.
The first input for SECT is deleting all stored sections in the database and in addition all results of the sections.

The sections have to be defined in a pure monotonic way with respect to NO and the XS value. Sections are belong together as one "beam" if they have the same number. So they can be displayed graphically with program WinGraf. SIR will maintain as default the last defined NO, the very first NO default to 1. The distance XS will be calculated from the difference to the last reference point (XM,YM,ZM) if a value for XS isnot given.
Every section is identified like a beam section with a number and an ordinate XS. The geometry of a section plane is described via:
the reference point of the plane (corresponds to the origin of the cross section)
2. a local coordinate system of the section normal vector of area = local x axis direction for the orientation of the y axis
a clipping window within the local coordinate system YMIN, YMAX, ZMIN, ZMAX
an active range for the supports (XMIN, XMAX)
The user defines the orientation of the local y axis with the item NR or the definition of the vector with the items SX, SY and SZ .
• no input for NR, SX, SY and SZ: The local z axis is aligned in the direction of gravity. If the normal of cut is parallel to the direction of gravity (column) the local y axis of the section
ZMIN Pp —X Sectional plane \ GLOBAL YMAX

Literal XX, YY, ZZ, NEGX, NEGY, NEGZ as input to NR:
The local y axis lies in a plane which is defined through the area normal and the global coordinate axis according to the above literal.
Input to SX, SY and SZ:
The local y axis lies in a plane which is defined through the area normal and the vector.

With the specification of an reference node at REF the reference point may be defined relatively to a structural node. With an input REF QUAD the reference point is defined relatively to the centre of the QUAD element NREF. Then the default for the local coordinate system is taken from the element itself.
If no reference material is input for the definition of the cross section in the input for the program AQUA, that one of the first intersected element is used.

If a section lies exactly along a QUAD element edge, the section will find then two QUAD elements. Only the element which lies behind the plane in the normal direction of the section plane is used then.
The warping moment Mb from QUAD elements is calculated only if the coordinates of the shear centre are input at YSC and ZSC.
if no record SECT is defined, the sections saved in the database are used, which can be defined with the program WINGRAF.
All sections are saved in the database. They can be checked and changed with the program WINGRAF.

The output of SIR consists of two tables for each section. The first table is optional and de- scribes the geometry of the section and of all intersected elements.
The second table lists the sum of all resultant section components for each load case. The user gets also the parts of all individual elements with ECHO FORC.
A graphical representation may be produced for every load case and every section component.
The individual components may be switched on or off with PLOT or the suboptions NX to W.

The section definition and the forces for each load are saved in the data base for a later inter- pretation. In this case all already existing SIR-dates in the data base are overwritten and/or deleted.

The type SUPPORTS with the sum of corresponding nodal forces and moments is printed additionally per load case in the list of the forces and moments considering ECHO REAC YES, FULL, EXTR or 4. All nodes inside the section box are used, independend of the group control. With ECHO REAC EXTR the resulting forces of bedding of the area elements are added. The used area elements are dependend from the group control. With ECHO REAC 4 the resulting forces of bedding of the area elements are used instead of the node support forces.

The results of SIR can be stored in an input file for the programs AQUA and AQBS for the use of a classical beam design. The kind and the extent of these dates are described with the corresponding CTRL options.
The corresponding force and moment distributions are represented graphically in Report Browser output with the input ECHO PLOT YES or ECHO NX to W YES.
